clue.text: Coins, including silver, added to account by one showing wisdom

indicators.note: the coins word is opened up to take in the other pieces, so including marks a container

parts.note: sous are old French coins of small value
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A wise person adds coins and some silver to their bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts AG, AC and I inside SOUS, the old French coins; 'added to' and 'by' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sagacious has keen judgement and good sense, which is what showing wisdom describes.

clue.text: Valve, firm under pressure, cutting supply

indicators.note: the pair of pieces cuts into the supply word, splitting it

parts.note: stock is a supply of goods

indicators.note: in a down clue the firm piece sits under the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A valve that holds firm under pressure stops the supply flowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' places CO below P in this down clue, and 'cutting' sets PCO inside STOCK.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopcock is a tap or valve controlling the flow in a pipe.

clue.text: Sports car getting round 20 lake in a flash

indicators.note: the car abbreviation gets round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: GT, gran turismo, is a type of sports car
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A sports car speeds round a lake in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a flash' reads as 'quickly', but 'in' is a piece and 'a flash' the definition. The stray '20' in the print plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: A glint is a brief gleam or sparkle of light.

clue.text: Character in Lear distressed about unfeeling 23

parts.note: a card is a character, an eccentric person

indicators.note: the jumbled name goes about the unfeeling word, enclosing it
distressed means damaged or upset, so the letters of the name are mixed up

parts.note: numb means without feeling

explanation.surface: A figure in Shakespeare's tragedy grieves over the cold-hearted Regan.
explanation.walkthrough: '23' looks like a reference to the Lear character at 23 down but is the number twenty-three itself. 'distressed' makes ALER of LEAR, and 'about' wraps it round NUMB.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-three is a counting number, the kind that states how many rather than a position.

clue.text: Work silly dopes resisted

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: silly suggests foolish disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Foolish dopes put up opposition to the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' makes POSED from DOPES, after OP.
explanation.definitionFit: To have opposed something is to have resisted or fought against it.

clue.text: Sign given by son with expression of surprise about price list

indicators.note: the surprise word goes about the price index letters, enclosing them

parts.note: coo is a British exclamation of surprise
RPI is the Retail Price Index, an index or list of prices

explanation.surface: A son gasps in surprise at a price list he is shown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coo!' is an old-fashioned British exclamation of surprise; the RPI, Britain's Retail Price Index, tracks prices. 'about' puts RPI inside COO.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Quizzes with music revolving around latest in charts

indicators.note: around says the music word turned backwards wraps the picked letter
revolving turns the music word round so it reads from the end

parts.note: ska is a Jamaican music style

indicators.note: the latest letter in the word charts is its final one

explanation.surface: A pop quiz show spins records and keeps track of the newest chart entries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolving' turns SKA into AKS, and 'around' puts S (the last letter of 'charts') inside it after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Quizzes as a verb means questions or interrogates someone, the same as putting questions.

clue.text: Audible rendition of musical work, proper confection

indicators.note: an audible rendition is how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: a suite is an instrumental work in several movements; meet is an old word meaning proper or fitting

explanation.surface: A performance of a piece of music, sweetened with something suitable.
explanation.walkthrough: SUITE is said as 'sweet' and MEET as 'meat'; 'meet' meaning proper is archaic, as in 'it is meet and right'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetmeat is a sweet delicacy such as candied fruit or a sugared treat.

clue.text: Not going to lose time speaking

indicators.note: the staying word loses a letter, which is removed

parts.note: someone not going is staying

explanation.surface: Someone stays put rather than waste time talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' takes T out of STAYING. 'speaking' fits as in 'so to speak': the definition and answer are both present participles.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is uttering it, the same act as speaking.

clue.text: Cut and run, for example rules?

definitions.text: Cut and run, for example rules?

parts.words: Cut and run, for example rules?
parts.note: cut and run look like an idiom for fleeing, but they are words whose past forms break the usual pattern; such words flout grammar's rules

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut and run' looks like the idiom for fleeing; take the words separately as verbs. Their past forms (cut, ran) do not add -ed, so they break the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbs whose past tense and participle do not follow the standard -ed pattern, as with cut and ran.

clue.text: Tree, larger than average? That's right

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, bigger than the usual sizes
That's read as 'that is', abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A question about whether a tree is bigger than usual, answered with a confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' expands to 'that is', whose abbreviation is IE; the question mark disguises the run of abbreviations as a query and its answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a willow, a tree grown for its pliant shoots used in basketry.

clue.text: Fitness expert with devotion set about run

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

indicators.note: the devotion word is set around the abbreviation for run, enclosing it

parts.note: piety is religious devotion
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A fitness trainer devoted to the job sets off for a jog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitness' looks like exercise, but here it means suitability. 'set about' puts R inside PIETY to give PRIETY, after PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Propriety is the quality of being proper or suitable, the fitness of conduct to the occasion.

clue.text: Spikes found in containers 27 holding assortment of kit

indicators.note: the containers word holds the jumbled letters inside it

parts.note: cans are tin containers

indicators.note: an assortment is a mixed selection, so the letters of kit are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone rummages in tins full of odds and ends of kit and finds some spikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assortment of' turns KIT into ATKI, which 'holding' puts inside CANS. The stray '27' in the print is a page artefact and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Catkins are the hanging flower spikes of trees such as willow and hazel.

clue.text: Quickly name county's administrative centre

parts.note: presto is the musical direction for a very quick tempo

explanation.surface: An instruction to hurry and name the seat of a county council.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESTON is the administrative centre of Lancashire, a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Lancashire city houses the county council, making it the county town.

clue.text: Part of spacecraft, protuberant part carrying I first bits of moon dust back after short interval 2

indicators.note: after says the bulge piece comes after the interval piece

parts.note: a comma is a tiny musical interval, and also a short pause

indicators.note: the bulge word carries the turned letters inside it

parts.note: a nodule is a small rounded lump that sticks out

indicators.note: back turns the picked pair round
the first bits of moon and dust are their opening letters

explanation.surface: A spacecraft's knobbly part picks up moon dust after a brief pause in the mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MD into DM, 'carrying' puts it inside NODULE, and 'after' sets that after COMMA. The stray 'I' and '2' in the print play no part.
explanation.definitionFit: The command module was the Apollo crew capsule, the section of the spacecraft that returned to Earth.

clue.text: Craft has bumped into vessel in which solemn-looking person is upset

parts.note: to have bumped into someone is to have met them

indicators.note: the vessel holds the turned bird word inside it

parts.note: an ark is a large boat

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: an owl is a person who looks solemn and wise

explanation.surface: A craft has crashed into a boat whose glum-faced passenger is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is upset' turns OWL into LWO, and 'in which' sets it inside ARK, after MET.
explanation.definitionFit: Metalwork is the craft of shaping metal into objects.

clue.text: Indolence I would lessen, given work

parts.note: I'd is the short form of I would

indicators.note: the letters of lessen are put to work and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lazy person would happily do less if given a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given work' rearranges LESSEN into LENESS, after ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness and indolence both mean laziness, avoiding work.

clue.text: Keep the reader involved and sympathetic

parts.note: to tend is to look after or keep

indicators.note: involved means tangled or intricate, so the letters of the phrase are tangled

explanation.surface: Advice to a writer: hold the reader's interest and show some compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' reworks THE READER into ERHEARTED, which follows TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tender-hearted means being easily moved to pity, which is what sympathetic describes.

clue.text: Non-indigenous plants coexist in peculiar fashion

indicators.note: a peculiar fashion is an odd arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Foreign plants live alongside native ones in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in peculiar fashion' rearranges the letters of COEXIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotics are plants introduced from abroad rather than native to the region.

clue.text: Ambassador receiving listen

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Ambassador receiving listen (7)': HE (ambassador) is the only wordplay, and nothing gives the ARKEN that the container needs; the clue appears cut short in the OCR.

clue.text: Walk about island, climbing to discover frozen region

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the pieces are read from the bottom up

parts.note: to pace is to walk
C is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A walk round an island, climbing to find an ice field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns PACE + C + I into ICECAP, reading upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An icecap is a permanent covering of ice over a large area, such as a polar region.

clue.text: Look to get into group, offering capital

indicators.note: the look word gets into the group word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a combo is a small band of musicians
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone tries to break into a band in the hope of making money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money; it is a city, COLOMBO, the commercial capital of Sri Lanka. 'to get into' puts LO inside COMBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombo is the largest city and commercial capital of Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Antagonistic counsel having one replaced with little hesitation

indicators.note: one letter in the counsel word is swapped out and the sound of hesitation put in its place

parts.note: to counsel is to advise
I is the Roman numeral for one
er is the short sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: A hostile lawyer who barely pauses before speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counsel' suggests a barrister but is the verb ADVISE; swapping its I for ER gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means opposed or hostile, the same as antagonistic.

clue.text: Character in Lear belonging to dire gang

indicators.note: belonging to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean figure who belongs to a terrible gang.
explanation.walkthrough: King Lear's cruel daughter fits a 'dire gang', so the surface suits her.
explanation.definitionFit: Regan is one of King Lear's two treacherous daughters in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Dig in front of courtyard and pierce flower

indicators.note: the front of courtyard is its first letter

parts.note: to dig something is slang for loving it
to pink is to pierce or prick, as with pinking shears or a sword

explanation.surface: A gardener digs at the front of the courtyard and pierces the soil to plant a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' is not spadework but 1960s slang for liking something, giving LOVE, which sits after C from 'front of courtyard'.
explanation.definitionFit: The clove pink is a clove-scented garden carnation, Dianthus caryophyllus.

clue.text: Villain with vigour doing volte-face, seized by regret

indicators.note: the regret word grabs the reversed piece and holds it inside

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: a volte-face is an about-turn, so the vigour word is turned round

parts.note: go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A villain loses his energy and turns penitent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing volte-face' turns GO into OG, and 'seized by' puts it inside RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest scoundrel, a villain.

clue.text: Position diver may adopt to get fish

definitions.meaning: a diving position with the body bent at the hips and legs straight

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: the jackknife diving position, and the long-snouted predator of rivers and lakes.

clue.text: Society, at home with G & S, repeatedly holding acceptable music events

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: the doubled pair of letters holds the acceptable word between its copies
repeatedly says the pair of letters appears twice

parts.note: G and S are given as letters, also the initials of Gilbert and Sullivan
on means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: A society that keeps putting on Gilbert and Sullivan at home holds musical evenings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'G & S' suggests Gilbert and Sullivan, the Victorian comic-opera pair, but gives just the letters G and S, doubled by 'repeatedly' with ON inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sing-songs are informal gatherings where people sing together.
